adversarial_review.check: The cited W2 theorem requires each onsite perturbation to be o(|x|^2) at infinity, whereas the Q3 double-well term has a positive quartic leading part and V(x)/|x|^2 tends to infinity.

The theorem requires Fourier-transform derivative distributions of orders two and three to be L1 functions; a quartic polynomial has a finite combination of delta derivatives instead, so the required L1 condition is not met.
The Q3-lock cross-site quartic polynomial is also outside the theorem's bounded-decay/Fourier-integrability perturbation class even if the quadratic bond is placed in the harmonic reference part.

The cited result concerns a suitable W2 observable algebra and commutator locality; it does not by itself provide the Q3 two-sided Gibbs split-history estimate or the common-alpha KMS quotient identification.
Hypothesis mismatch is only an applicability boundary and does not prove nonexistence of a quartic Q3 dynamics or a different weighted topology.
No exact-Q3 generator, heat_root_incidence owner, Sector A composition, or physical reference is supplied by this literature audit.
